title: NASA ARSET — Satellite Remote Sensing for Agricultural Applications
provider: NASA Applied Remote Sensing Training Program (ARSET), under NASA Applied Sciences / Earthdata
language: English and Spanish (all slides and homework provided in both; live webinars delivered in English with Spanish-language materials)
cost: Free ($0). No registration fee; all slides, Q&A transcripts, and homework are open-access.
certificate: ARSET issues certificates of completion for attendees who attend all live sessions and complete the homework assignments (standard ARSET policy). The specific course page does not state certificate criteria verbatim — set as ARSET-standard but [UNVERIFIED] for this exact offering.
duration: Four weeks (April 14 – May 5, 2020); four live webinar sessions of 1.5 hours each (~6 hours total live instruction), plus two homework assignments.
level: Introductory. Prerequisite: ARSET "Fundamentals of Remote Sensing" course.
target_audience: Local, state, federal, private, and non-governmental organizations involved in agricultural monitoring, agricultural policy, food security, agricultural insurance, and humanitarian relief.
format: Online instructor-led live webinar series — four Tuesday sessions, each 1.5 hours, with live Q&A. Recordings, slides, and Q&A transcripts archived for self-paced viewing afterward. NOT a hands-on coding course; it is a data-product / data-access / case-study briefing series.
assessment: Two homework assignments delivered via Google Forms: Homework 1 (assigned in Part 1, due April 28, 2020) and Homework 2 (assigned in Part 3, due May 12, 2020). Spanish versions of both homeworks provided. Homework completion plus attendance is the basis for ARSET certificates.
hands_on: Minimal / none. This is a conceptual webinar focused on data discovery, data access, and decision-making case studies — not on code exercises. Participants learn how to locate and acquire products (e.g., SMAP soil moisture, LDAS, ET/ESI) and interpret them, but there are no Google Earth Engine scripts or Jupyter/Colab notebooks bundled with this specific course. Homework is form-based (data-acquisition and interpretation questions) rather than programming.
tools: Missions/sensors: Landsat (record since 1972), SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive). Data products: SMAP soil moisture, NASA Land Data Assimilation System (LDAS) soil moisture & shallow groundwater, evapotranspiration (ET), Evaporative Stress Index (ESI). Programs referenced: NASA HARVEST. Monitored parameters: precipitation, temperature, evapotranspiration, soil moisture, vegetation health. No GEE, Python, or QGIS used in this introductory course.

syllabus.module: Part 1 — Overview of Agricultural Remote Sensing (Apr 14, 2020)
syllabus.topics: History of Earth observations for agriculture; satellites and sensors usable for agriculture; limitations of satellite data; introduction to NASA HARVEST; examples of current EO applications in agriculture; live Q&A. Materials: slides (74.1 MB PDF, EN; 13.4 MB ES), Q&A transcript, Homework 1.

syllabus.module: Part 2 — Soil Moisture for Agricultural Applications (Apr 21, 2020)
syllabus.topics: Overview of SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive); agricultural case studies using SMAP; soil moisture and shallow groundwater from the Land Data Assimilation System (LDAS); live Q&A. Materials: slides (88.1 MB PDF, EN; 5.6 MB ES), Q&A transcript.

syllabus.module: Part 3 — Earth Observations for Agricultural Monitoring (Apr 28, 2020)
syllabus.topics: Review of related/previous ARSET trainings relevant to agricultural monitoring; case studies of EO used for crop and agricultural monitoring; live Q&A. Materials: slides (80.4 MB PDF, EN; 4.7 MB ES), Q&A transcript, Homework 2 (due May 12).

syllabus.module: Part 4 — Evapotranspiration (ET) and Evaporative Stress Index (ESI) for Agricultural Applications (May 5, 2020)
syllabus.topics: Guest-speaker presentation; overview of ET and ESI; agricultural and drought case studies; live Q&A. Materials: slides (9.4 MB PDF, EN; 32.9 MB ES), Q&A transcript.

strengths: Genuinely $0-cost and fully open-access (slides, recordings, Q&A transcripts, homework) — matches FOLUR's zero-budget constraint exactly.
Fully bilingual delivery (English + Spanish) with parallel homework — proves a workable model for non-English audiences, directly relevant to FOLUR's Russian-language requirement.
Clearly scoped, modular 4-part structure (1.5h each) with explicit learning objectives — low cognitive load, easy to schedule for working professionals/SMB.
Audience definition is decision-maker / practitioner oriented (policy, insurance, food security, humanitarian) rather than academic — same practitioner framing FOLUR needs for agro-SMB.
Strong emphasis on data DISCOVERY and ACCESS (where to find SMAP/LDAS/ET products and how to acquire them) — a transferable, tool-agnostic skill.
Case-study-driven: each thematic session anchors concepts in real applications (drought, crop monitoring, humanitarian response).
Explicit prerequisite chaining ('Fundamentals of Remote Sensing' first) gives a clean learning pathway.
Homework delivered via free Google Forms — a zero-infrastructure assessment mechanism FOLUR could mirror.
weaknesses: No hands-on coding: zero Google Earth Engine, Python, or Colab exercises — learners cannot DO crop analysis after this course, only understand concepts. FOLUR's audience needs executable skills, which this course does not deliver.
Dataset emphasis is US/NASA-centric (SMAP, LDAS, HARVEST) with coarse-resolution soil-moisture products less suited to field-scale SMB decisions in North Kazakhstan.
Content is from 2020 — predates current GEE/cloud workflows and newer Sentinel-based methods; some product links and tooling may be dated.
Webinar/lecture format with form-based homework gives weak skill verification — no graded notebooks or reproducible artifacts proving competence.
Very large slide PDFs (74–88 MB) are a real barrier for low-bandwidth rural users — a delivery anti-pattern FOLUR should avoid.
No QGIS or open-desktop GIS component, so it does not cover the visualization tooling FOLUR's $0 stack relies on.
Certificate criteria not stated on the course page itself (ARSET-standard assumption only).
borrow_for_folur: Заимствовать тематическую модульную структуру 4×1.5ч с явными learning objectives на каждый модуль — низкая когнитивная нагрузка, удобно для работающих представителей МСБ.
Перенять модель полностью двуязычной выдачи материалов (у NASA — EN/ES) как доказанный шаблон для русскоязычной аудитории СКО/Костанай/Акмола: слайды + конспект Q&A + домашка на одном языке.

Использовать тематические блоки как карту: влажность почвы (аналог SMAP/LDAS), эвапотранспирация и индекс водного стресса (ET/ESI) для оценки засухи, мониторинг состояния посевов — это прямые сценарии для агро-МСБ Северного Казахстана; в FOLUR заменить продукты NASA на бесплатные Sentinel-1/2 + GEE/Colab аналоги.

Перенять акцент на НАВЫК ПОИСКА И ДОСТУПА к данным (где найти продукт, как его скачать) как отдельную обучаемую компетенцию — но реализовать через GEE Data Catalog и открытые порталы (Copernicus, ASF), а не NASA Earthdata.

Заимствовать бесплатный механизм оценки через Google Forms как нулевой-инфраструктурный вариант — но в FOLUR УСИЛИТЬ его автогрейдингом ноутбуков (у платформы уже есть engine/autograder), чтобы закрыть слабую верификацию навыка у ARSET.

Перенять кейс-ориентированную подачу (каждая тема = реальный сценарий: засуха, классификация культур, страхование урожая) и заземлить на реальные данные СКО/Костанай/Акмола вместо абстрактных примеров.

ИЗ СМЕЖНОГО, БОЛЕЕ СИЛЬНОГО КУРСА ARSET (Crop Mapping using SAR & Optical RS / Crop Classification) заимствовать практическую педагогику, которой нет в данном вводном курсе: готовые Jupyter-ноутбуки (.ipynb) + zip с imagery и vector data через Google Drive, GitHub-репозиторий, и пошаговые инструкции 'повтори упражнение самостоятельно' на Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 — это и есть hands-on GEE/Colab-модель для FOLUR.
Заимствовать чёткую цепочку предпосылок (сначала 'Основы ДЗЗ', потом прикладной курс) для выстраивания траектории А-модулей FOLUR.
АНТИ-паттерн для избегания: не публиковать слайды по 70–90 МБ; для сельской аудитории с низкой пропускной способностью дробить материалы и хостить на GitHub Pages в лёгком виде.
